title: Why is Monday night's game so significant to Saints history?
description: The Saints are celebrating one of the biggest moments in team history on Monday night. As they should.
fullText:
Roughly 21 years ago, Category 5 Hurricane Katrina made landfall in New Orleans and devastated Louisiana's biggest city. The storm killed nearly 1,400 people and caused $125 billion in damage. The greater New Orleans community took years to recover from the natural disaster. Even the beloved New Orleans Saints were forced to play their home games elsewhere during the 2005 season because of extensive damage to the famous Louisiana Superdome.

A Week 3 home game against the Atlanta Falcons in 2006 marked the Saints' return to a rebuilt Superdome, with the people of New Orleans still healing from Katrina. When the Saints blew the Falcons out 23-3 during an emotional evening, the night quickly became the biggest and most important night in franchise history. You probably most remember the game for ALS survivor Steve Gleason, who blocked a punt that was recovered for a touchdown within the first two minutes of the first quarter and set the tone for a raucous night:

THE SAINTS BLOCK THE PUNT!!

Steve Gleason came flying in for a perfect block leading to Curtis DeLoatch falling on it in the end zone.

The Superdome is as loud as it’s ever been right now. What a moment for the city of New Orleans! https://t.co/BkvdiNtcgx pic.twitter.com/V0tiSO7D1k

This Monday night's matchup between the Saints and Falcons isn't exactly on the anniversary of that famous game. (That would be September 25th, 2006, for what it is worth.) But it is close enough for the Saints to celebrate one of the most memorable victories they'll ever have. That's why you're seeing so much celebration and remembrance for the game during ESPN's coverage of Saints-Falcons.

According to the Saints, the night will include, among other things, a pregame interview with NBC's Mike Tirico, who called that famous post-Katrina Saints game for ESPN. New Orleans native and actor Anthony Mackie will narrate a special opening for the night. There will also be a video of Gleason, commemorating his blocked punt, with recent Hall of Fame inductee quarterback and fellow franchise legend Drew Brees joining a "Who Dat" chant from the field.

The Saints understand their history and how much that fateful 2006 Monday night game meant to the city of New Orleans. Kudos to them for pulling out all the stops to celebrate it with their community.

title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander believes Russell Westbrook has 'little bit more in the tank'
description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander believes Russell Westbrook has 'little bit more in the tank.'
fullText:
This past August was the latest sign of our fragile mortality. In the early waves of the 2010s era-defining NBA superstars calling it quits, Russell Westbrook announced his retirement. After an epic 18-season career, he hung up his sneakers for good as one of the most polarizing names ever.

When Westbrook announced his NBA retirement, current players and all-time legends showed their love. Several flooded his social media post that broke the news. Heck, even Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ended his years-long Twitter hiatus to wish him the best.

Of course, Gilgeous-Alexander and Westbrook are linked for the rest of basketball eternity. Even if they never shared a locker room together. When you think of some of the greatest and best Thunder players of all time, those two are top of the top three names. Alongside Kevin Durant.

Westbrook spent his first 11 seasons on the Thunder. That's where he enjoyed his best years. Both on an individual and team level. The former MVP broke the mystique surrounding the triple-double in OKC. Along the way, he was a perennial All-Star/All-NBA member. He also co-starred in several of their deep playoff runs.

Gilgeous-Alexander talked 

"He is as dynamic as they come in terms of an NBA player, personality and teammate. Russ is the whole package. He's the foundation for what we stand on now," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "Part of the reason why the city is what it is is because of Russell Westbrook. He deserves all those flowers for what he's done off the court and on the court."

Now, the timing of Westbrook's NBA retirement caught most of the basketball world a little off guard. After all, he averaged 15.2 points, 6.7 assists and 5.4 rebounds in his final season last year on the Sacramento Kings. Surely a team could use that type of production, no? Well, the market wasn't rich enough for the 37-year-old. Instead of settling, he left of his own accord.

Either way, milking an extra year of his legendary career would've done very little for him, in my opinion. Good to leave the game before the game leaves you. "What he's done for the game of basketball, for the kids, for the city, for the world, has been special," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "And we'll miss Russ."

title: Guelph Storm forward Parker Snelgrove out indefinitely after injury
description: The Guelph Storm have lost Parker Snelgrove for an indefinite amount of time after surgery suffered in a recent game
fullText:
The Guelph Storm have announced that forward Parker Snelgrove will be out of action, undergoing surgery for a fractured ankle.

Snelgrove, 19, was injured early in Guelph's game Sunday against the Kitchener Rangers, having left in the first period and not returning to the ice.

An update was not immediately had regarding the status of Snelgrove. The Storm did not give a timeline for how long Snelgrove could be out, but that the team will update when the surgery is had.

Snelgrove in his fourth OHL season, having been a second round pick of Guelph in the 2023 OHL Priority Selection, 30th overall. Snelgrove has appeared in 191 games for the Storm, with 23 goals, 35 assists, & 58 points. Snelgrove has a point in six games for Guelph this season.

Guelph loses a hole in their bottom-six with the absence of Snelgrove, a veteran center who has shown flashes of offense in his depth role, although the Storm have enough security down the middle with Jaakko Wycisk, Tyler Hopkins, & Owen Griffin in the depth chart.

The Storm have a 4-2-0 record on the season with Hopkins leading Guelph's offense with nine points in four games since returning from Toronto Maple Leafs training camp.

title: Oklahoma ranked as a middle-of-the-pack SEC team by ESPN's FPI
description: ESPN's FPI ranks Oklahoma No. 9 in the SEC, putting the Sooners firmly in the conference's middle tier.
fullText:
While the 2026 college football season hasn't gone the way the Oklahoma Sooners wanted, there is still plenty of time to make it memorable. The Sooners are 2-2, with losses to the Michigan Wolverines and the Georgia Bulldogs, and a narrow 14-6 win over the New Mexico Lobos.

The Sooners' offense has been a major disappointment this season. Star quarterback John Mateer has struggled with turnovers this season. He's turned it over six times in the last three games. Due to those struggles, the optimism from last season's College Football Playoff run has started to fade.

In fact, ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI) measures team strength and is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance for the rest of the season. It ranks the Sooners No. 9 in the SEC after the bye week.

While being ranked No. 9 in the SEC by the SEC is far from where Oklahoma expected to be entering the season, the Sooners still have an opportunity to change that outlook. The bye week gave the team a chance to reset, and now Oklahoma has perhaps the perfect opportunity to prove the projections wrong with the No. 1 Texas Longhorns waiting in the Red River Rivalry.

A win over the Longhorns would immediately change the conversation surrounding the Sooners and could provide the momentum needed for a strong second half. Oklahoma may not control where the FPI ranks it, but it can control what happens on the field, and Saturday gives the Sooners a chance to start rewriting the 2026 season's story.

title: Warriors' Stephen Curry Reveals What He's Seen From Brandin Podziemski
description: Following the Warriors 101-104 loss to the LA Clippers on Sunday, Stephen Curry discussed the growth he's seen from Brandin Podziemski
fullText:
Brandin Podziemski had a rough shooting night for the Golden State Warriors in their 101-104 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday, Oct. 4. Podziemski went 2-for-10 from the field, as most of the Warriors' roster spent the game trying to find their range. Yet, despite the Warriors' loss and Podziemski's poor shooting, the coaching staff will undoubtedly be pleased with the increased aggression and decisiveness he displayed throughout the game.

This summer, the discussion around Podziemski's development has centered on his willingness to take more threes and be more aggressive when looking for his shot. However, that won't be the only thing Podziemski has been working on this summer, as he continues to refine his game and look for areas to improve.

Speaking to the media after Golden State's preseason defeat, Stephen Curry shared what he's seen from Podziemski during training camp and the areas of growth that he's noticed.

"Same player, same talent," Curry said. "He looks like he's in better shape. He looks a little stronger, a little quicker. And then it's about putting all those skill sets together and making him be decisive on the court when he's out there. Shooting the shots he knows he's supposed to shoot, not turning down threes if he's open, making the right play. I know he's very determined. I know I talked to him during camp, and he said he had a great summer of making sure his body was right... He's obviously had a great camp, especially offensively. I want that to continue."

Podziemski projects to have a sizeable role for the Warriors this season. He'll likely be part of Kerr's starting rotation and tasked with being a connective piece on both ends of the floor. Golden State will likely hope he can up his decisiveness on offense and continue to remain healthy; then, if his development continues to trend upward, his role could scale as the season goes on.

title: Milwaukee Bucks open preseason vs. Minnesota Timberwolves | Live updates
description: The Milwaukee Bucks open up their 2026-27 preseasons schedule vs. the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 5, 2026. Check for roster updates and odds.
fullText:
The Milwaukee Bucks open their five-game exhibition slate tonight at Fiserv Forum when they face the new-look Minnesota Timberwolves. The Bucks, of course, are also a very different team this season on the court, beginning with new head coach Taylor Jenkins.

Jenkins is overseeing an overhauled roster as well, as the team traded franchise legend Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami in the offseason for four players and a handful of draft picks, including rookie Nate Ament.

Minnesota features new point guard LaMelo Ball, who was the Timberwolves' top acquisition in the offseason.

Jenkins said that while all 21 players are available against Minnesota, not all will play. Jenkins said he anticipates about 13 players to set foot on the court, depending on how the game unfolds. He wanted some of his regulars to play longer, though not until the fourth quarter.

Earlier in the week, Jenkins hinted that he might play different starting lineups through the five-game exhibition slate, but he amended that before the game against the Timberwolves and said he didn't anticipate five unique combinations to begin the games.

"Don't hold me to it but I could see us having a different starting lineup in the next two games [at Oklahoma City and at Charlotte] and some of our guys won't play all five games," he said. "It's going to be a day-to-day process."

He said some players will play two stints and some will play three and a few will be worked into the third quarter.

"Want to just get an initial sample size, not go too extreme with the work load and the minute totals and then just slowly continue to ramp up day-to-day and game-by-game," Jenkins said.

Tipoff for the Bucks-Timerwolves Oct. 5 preseason game is scheduled for 7 p.m.

The Bucks have moved its games over-the-air this season, and it will be broadcast in the Milwaukee area on MY24 with Lisa Byington, Marques Johnson and Melanie Ricks on the call.

During the preseason, there are no formal injury reports. Through the Bucks' open practice on Oct. 3, head coach Taylor Jenkins had said every player was participating in practices.

Here are the upcoming games for Milwaukee:

Oct. 7 at Oklahoma City, 7 p.m. CT

Oct. 11 at Charlotte, 6 p.m. CT

Minnesota is a 5.5-point favorite and the over/under is set at 230.5 points, per BetMGM.

fullText:
Kansas State athletic director breaks silence on $12 million Jerome Tang settlement appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Kansas State basketball ended the Jerome Tang era in rough fashion during the offseason. Which now includes the Wildcats putting together a $12 million settlement with Tang. Now KSU athletic director Gene Taylor spoke out about the move Monday.

ESPN college basketball insider Pete Thamel shared a succinct statement via Taylor.

"This settlement allows both parties to move forward on agreed terms," Thamel posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

So KSU canned Tang nearly seven months ago, with the move deemed a firing for cause. Yet Tang was owed $18.7 million per his contract with the Big 12 University. And that deal was originally set to run through the 2030-2031 season.

The Wildcats and Taylor still orchestrated the move to fire Tang, largely due to the late season collapse. Kansas State went 10-15 the rest of the way and missed out on landing a bid inside March Madness.

Tang, though, ruffled some feathers with the fan base and the school following some widely critical remarks he made after an embarrassing 91-62 loss to Cincinnati in conference play. Saying how the KSU players "did not deserve to wear this uniform" while also repeatedly saying how "embarrassed" he was by the performance.

He even vowed that most of the players from last year's roster wouldn't return. Those comments eventually led to Tang's falling out with the university.

Tang added another twist to this case: Hiring the attorneys who represented Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss amid his NCAA eligibility case. Now KSU and Tang have moved forward from its exit.

title: ‘Did Not Think This Would Actually Happen,’ ‘Backfield Gets Even Messier’ — NFL World Has Mixed Reactions to Joe Mixon Signing With Seahawks After Mystery Injury
description: The Seattle Seahawks are in the process of adding running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after working him out Monday, coach Mike Macdonald said, and early takes from people on social media weighed his health against Seattle’s crowded backfield. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Monday that Seattle is signing Mixon, who will wear jersey No.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks are in the process of adding running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after working him out Monday, coach Mike Macdonald said, and early takes from people on social media weighed his health against Seattle's crowded backfield.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on Monday that Seattle is signing Mixon, who will wear jersey No. 25. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the plan is to sign the veteran running back to the practice squad once he completes his medical exam.

Mixon, a two-time Pro Bowler, missed all of 2025 with a foot injury, and the Houston Texans released him in March. Texans general manager Nick Caserio called the injury "kind of a freak thing" in January.

In July, KPRC-2 Houston's Aaron Wilson reported that Mixon had told former Bengals teammates he was done playing and that he had dealt with blood flow problems in his foot and had recently undergone another surgery on it. He added that a source close to Mixon still saw some hope of a return.

SleeperSeahawks, a Seahawks news account, was struck by how quickly things changed over the last 48 hours. "He must be healthy!" SleeperSeahawks wrote.

Fox Sports' Jay Glazer had reported a day earlier that Seattle was bringing Mixon in for a visit. Schultz reported later Monday that Seattle wanted to make sure Mixon was in shape and came away impressed with his conditioning, and that Mixon will start on the practice squad.

For The Latest Information: NFL Injury Report

A fan drew the same conclusion about the foot. "They wouldn't sign Mixon if the foot was bad," the fan wrote, adding that a healthy Mixon could earn a real role fast.

Mixon was productive the last time he played. He ran for 1,016 yards, 15th in the NFL, and 11 touchdowns on 245 carries for Houston in 2024, and he has 7,428 career rushing yards in 111 games. His last game was a Divisional Round playoff game at Kansas City on Jan. 18, 2025.

Seattle ON Tap, a Seattle sports fan account, expressed surprise and hope for a healthy Mixon in his prime. "Did not think this would actually happen," Seattle ON Tap wrote.

Seattle also has a need at the position. The defending Super Bowl champions, 3-1 after Sunday's 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, put first-round rookie Jadarian Price on injured reserve Saturday with a chest injury, and Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs in March.

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer

One fan, replying to Schefter's report, wrote that a practice-squad start for a two-time Pro Bowler shows Seattle "wants to see the legs before handing him anything." The fan called it a low-risk move with Price on injured reserve.

Mixon would join the backfield Emanuel Wilson carried against the Chargers. Wilson, who is ranked 42nd on PFN's RB Impact Metric, ran 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and caught three passes for 39 yards and another score, while George Holani had 18 yards on seven carries.

Sports analyst Max Loeb, eager to see how the group looks with Charbonnet due back soon, still sided with the incumbent. "Adding him in Fantasy if my team is in a good spot/I have the room, still feel like it's Wilson's backfield," Loeb wrote.

Wilson has 190 yards on 53 carries through Week 4, an average of 3.6 per carry. According to Next Gen Stats, his rush yards over expected stand at -19 through Week 4, tying him for 36th among 45 qualified rushers.

FantasyPros analyst Derek Brown was blunter. "A mess of a backfield gets even messier," Brown wrote.

Charbonnet is working back, too. He tore his ACL in January's Divisional Round win over the San Francisco 49ers, had surgery on Feb. 20, and returned to practice Thursday.

"He's going to get team reps this week, which is really exciting," Macdonald told Seattle Sports' Brock and Salk on Monday. He also said Charbonnet will not play against the 49ers in Week 5.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Seattle has until Oct. 22 to add Charbonnet to the 53-man roster, or he must remain on the physically unable to perform list for the rest of the season.

Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Yahoo's fantasy account, poked fun at the logjam.

"Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet fantasy managers watching the Seahawks sign Joe Mixon," Yahoo Fantasy Sports wrote.

Mixon is not headed straight to the active roster. Macdonald said he would join the practice squad, and Schefter reported that Mixon was still completing his medical exam on Monday.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Fantasy football podcast host and writer Brian Drake went further. "Whenever an agent uses the word "talented" in their insider leaks, you know it's over. Mixon is toast. Don't bother adding him in fantasy," Drake wrote, telling fantasy managers not to bother adding him and pointing them to Wilson, Holani and Charbonnet instead.

The Seahawks host the 4-0 49ers on Sunday without Price or Charbonnet, then face the Denver Broncos four days later.

title: What I’m hearing at Gillette Stadium: Monday buzz (Week 5)
description: After an exciting win over the Buffalo Bills, the Patriots returned to Foxborough for a well-deserved Victory Monday.
fullText:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass — It was Victory Monday at Gillette Stadium, with the New England Patriots having earned the day to recover and celebrate the big win.

But, there were still some unanswered questions remaining following the game, and head coach Mike Vrabel spoke with reporters, answering a bunch of them.

Here's what I'm hearing at Gillette Stadium today:

Mack Hollins, who has been one of Drake Maye's favorite targets after losing A.J. Brown, departed Sunday's win early due to an injury, and on Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel was asked if he had an update. While he didn't say anything definitively, he did make it sound like Hollins missing this week is a possibility.

"I think we'll probably know more here in a little bit. I don't know if he'll be able to practice here for a couple days, but again, I don't have every detail," he said. "I'll get in there with Jim [Whalen] here afterwards and kind of see where we are and then make sure we have guys that are ready to go. Everybody's preparing as a starter. We know the energy that Mack brings, and next guy has to be ready to go."

Brown isn't eligible to return until next week, and then, without Hollins, the wide receiver room is a bit thin. So, could they explore adding someone?

"Sure. Anybody that can help us," Vrabel said. "We'll go explore here shortly."

Efton Chism's one-handed, game-winning touchdown catch is one that will be remembered for a long time. The young receiver earned a spot on the roster last season as a UDFA, and the same occured this summer. And due to injuries, Chism saw an increased role that led to the viral moment.

So, has he earned more time on the field?

"Sure, of course. That's what happens," Vrabel said. "I mean, guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities, they get more opportunities. I mean, we've been finding ways to work Chis in there previously. And it's a balance, but he certainly did a lot of things well. I know that he'll continue to do things well for us and continue to know a bunch of different spots."

After a lackluster performance in the first three weeks, Drake Maye looked much more like himself in the win, and because of his efforts, he was awarded a game ball in the locker room by his head coach.

"The thing to me is, we fumbled the snap, it's a mistake. But we picked the ball up, we stayed alive and we hit an X-play. So, I think that really has to exemplify what we want to be, who we want to be as a team and who we want to be as an organization," Vrabel explained. "There's going to be things that happen, things that we don't plan for. But certainly, the play isn't over, the game isn't over, and I think that really sums up everything that we want to do. So, I think that was a huge moment for us of just saying, "Hey, pick the ball up and go try to find a way to make a play, a positive play," but also figure out why the quarterback-center exchange is – we had the ball on the ground twice."

As for the two fumbled snaps, Vrabel said they "have to practice it and continue to practice it."

"Sometimes things happen," he added. "So, I know he's trying to get off the line of scrimmage. In our haste to get off the line of scrimmage, we have to stay in there and secure the snap. So, we'll continue to focus on those things. We have to be good in critical situations: short yardage, low red zone. When it gets tough, we have to be really good."

In the losses to the Seahawks and the Jaguars, as well as the win over the Steelers, the biggest issue appeared to be Maye's confidence. This time he was running with the ball and throwing it with certainty and confidence.

"I can try to help his confidence and show him things that he does that should make him confident. But ultimately, that's on each and every player," Vrabel said. "I think that gets built throughout the week, how you feel about certain plays, certain looks or how things looked in practice. And that's all we want to try to do, is what the players feel they have confidence in, to be able to run with speed, be aggressive and be decisive. So, that's why we put the plays in, that those are the ones that we feel like they have confidence in, and then they practice them throughout the week. So, that's what everybody's striving for and that's what we'll have to try to continue to do moving forward in order to improve."

One of the biggest strengths of the Patriots' defensive game plan was neutralizing Dalton Kincaid and not allowing Josh Allen to connect with him. It clearly threw the Bills off their game.

"I think awareness. I think that [Robert] Spillane did a nice job. On one play, they tried to hide him over there on the line of scrimmage," Vrabel stated. "It's not where he usually hangs out, and so he ran the over, and Spillane was able to carry him, I think, just long enough for Josh to go in a different direction. Felt like good coverage all day, being able to mix zone and mix man. But having an awareness of where he is and not letting him just run free."

And this is especially helpful as the Patriots will have their hands full with another very talented tight end this week.

"Again, they're feeding their tight ends. They have a great group," he said of the Raiders. "Certainly different play styles, but Brock (Bowers) is as elite as they come at that position. So, we'll have a huge challenge. We'll just be getting started here in a little bit."

Linebacker Erick Hunter slotted in on special teams at the gunner position and made a major tackle in the game.

"Thought he did fantastic. I thought Erick's really progressed every day since he's been here," Vrabel explained. "I think Jeremy [Springer] and Tom [Quinn] have done a fantastic job of working with him in our special teams, and he's trying to work with our defensive coaches. A lot of new things for Erick, and he's willing, he's got a really good length and he can run. We just figured, as we get guys that are down, we need bodies or DBs have to play or go down, why don't we give Erick a try? He didn't disappoint."

Similar to Maye, Doubs has also had a slower start to the season, but he has come alive in the last two weeks and has become one of the quarterback's trusted targets. It showed as he was on the receiving end of both fourth-down conversions as well as two of the three passing touchdowns.

"Yeah, it was great. I think that Rome puts a lot of pressure on himself to perform, like most players and most people that try to excel at a high level," Vrabel said. "I think that for him to not have a great play and to be able to come back is everything that we want to be able to do. We have the power to choose our response. When things happen, there's a moment in there where we get to choose. And so, I think his response to some of those plays have been really good."

For the third game in a row, the Patriots had a new player starting at right guard. So, how did he do and do they anticipate him starting there again this coming week?

"That's probably too quick for me to answer right now, just being less than 24 hours after the game, as far as a roster spot or positions," Vrabel stated. "But I thought Ben competed. I thought he did what Ben normally does. He goes in there and fights, and that's what I love about Ben, and that's what everybody on this team loves about Ben."

Last week, following the Patriots' loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Vrabel said he wants to see more from the interior defensive line. This week, they stepped up big time.

"I felt like those guys, especially early on, stopping the run. This was a team that could get the run going pretty quickly. But I think Milt [Milton Williams] factored, was disruptive and did a nice job with his hands. Cory [Durden], DaQuan [Jones], Josh [Farmer] and Lenny [Leonard Taylor III], they all had a role," Vrabel said. "I thought the outside linebackers did a nice job. I think they just continue to develop, especially looking at Gabe [Jacas] improving. I'm proud of the way that they all played, and I'm proud of the efforts, seeing how many guys got to the football, being able to hammer the football out and look at those chances.

"They hit a couple plays down the field, hit an X-play when he pump faked Gabe. We didn't get him on the ground down the middle of the field, but those are the plays that they're going to make. But we also forced their MVP quarterback to throw the ball behind his head that should've been returned for a pick-6. So, they did a lot of really good things, and we'll have to continue to do that as we move forward."

title: Washington Wizards 2026-27 Preseason Preview
description: The Washington Wizards are entering a new era. After starting the rebuild process in 2023, the Wizards threw themselves into the deep end and lost…a lot. They dropped at least 64 games for three straight seasons and won just 17 in 2025-26. But through the dark years, Washington has gained young talent, the No. 1 […] The post Washington Wizards 2026-27 Preseason Preview appeared first on The Lead.
fullText:
The Washington Wizards are entering a new era. After starting the rebuild process in 2023, the Wizards threw themselves into the deep end and lost…a lot. They dropped at least 64 games for three straight seasons and won just 17 in 2025-26. But through the dark years, Washington has gained young talent, the No. 1 pick, and stars for cheap.

It acquired Trae Young for CJ McCollum and Corey Kispert a month before the trade deadline. The next month, Washington brought home Anthony Davis and others for Khris Middleton, AJ Johnson, Malaki Branham, Marvin Bagley III, and draft capital. Young played five games in Wizards colors, while Davis is yet to suit up.

The Wizards used their first No. 1 overall selection since 2010 on AJ Dybantsa. The BYU forward led the nation in scoring and did it through unique athleticism and jump shooting. They also used the offseason to bring in some complementary pieces to add more depth to the roster.

Last season wasn't pretty, but the pieces are in place to ascend and leave the reconstruction chapter; 2026-27 will answer if playoff basketball returns to the capital.

30 teams in 30 days: Washington Wizards pic.twitter.com/FUvFzPCIE2

— Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) September 24, 2026

Washington traded Cam Whitmore to the Cleveland Cavaliers and received Tre Mann and a 2027 second-round pick in August. Whitmore's departure being the biggest hit to the Wizards' roster says something.

He played just 21 games off the bench for Washington as he was limited by a blood clot injury in his right shoulder. In Whitmore's 16.9 minutes on the floor, he averaged 9.2 points per game on 45.6% shooting — solid production. But in a depth chart with Dybantsa, Bilal Coulibaly, Will Riley, and Kyshawn George ahead of him, Whitmore wasn't going to be utilized. Cleveland waived him and Denver picked him up.

The move wasn't extremely popular among Wizards fans. Mann played just 66 games in the last two seasons. Last year, he competed for 12.6 minutes per contest and shot an unideal 36% from the field. He has shown flashes of potential, like his 14 points per game for Charlotte in 2024-25, albeit in just 14 appearances.

Losing Whitmore for Mann and a second-rounder may not have been a step forward, but it may not be a step back either, depicting how positive Washington's summer was.

— Hoop Central (@TheHoopCentral) December 2, 2025

Questions surrounded who Washington would select at No. 1 this June. While it wasn't clear who would have their name called, there was no doubt they'd be a generational talent. That's exactly what Dybantsa is.

Washington may be starting the beginning of a historic chapter in the franchise's history from day one of Dybantsa's career because of his sheer talent. The forward averaged 25.5 points per game on 51% shooting in his lone year as a Cougar.

His playstyle drew scouts' and fans' attention for a reason. Dybantsa can break down his defender on the perimeter with a hesitation or crossover, then choose his options from there: beat his next man with a sidestep to the lane, or fool him with a pivot and fadeaway jumper.

He scored at least 30 points eight times, two of which he scored at least 40. His 40 against Kansas State broke Kevin Durant's Big 12 Tournament freshman single-game scoring record. Dybantsa took the acclaim to the league, where he scored 27 points in his Summer League debut. That tied the most ever by a No. 1 pick.

He has the frame and athleticism of the all-time great scorers and is projected to rise near that level.

Dybantsa could win Rookie of the Year this season, which says a lot with the class he's competing with. First-year players of his caliber come in and change things in an instant, often making their team look brand new.

He doesn't just benefit Washington in 2027, but for years to come.

AJ Dybantsa Summer League Tape — 2 games pic.twitter.com/jRxCt4PQBT

— Basketball Performances (@NBAPerformances) July 22, 2026

Washington is an unproven team that looks incredible on paper. It has phenomenal pieces, but they've never been laid out on the board together. Can they fit to solve the puzzle that is the Wizards? The best-case scenario assumes they all do.

That means both chemistry and individual performance fall in line. It could look like Trae Young blending with Alex Sarr and Davis in the pick-and-roll while returning to efficient jump shooting. Or Davis' spacing working with Sarr's and keeping healthy. Even Dybantsa being able to contribute ROTY figures while Young and Tre Johnson still put up shots.

What follows is the quieter Wiz-Kids finally putting it together: Bub Carrington learns how to drive and defend, Coulibaly finds his shot, and Will Riley unlocks his brewing potential. Lastly, head coach Brian Keefe substantiates his position at the helm of the Wizards. The only years he's coached, Washington aimed to fail in. A productive season shows he has the answers to his first real test.

If all bodes well, Washington makes the playoffs for the first time in six years, and its ceiling is as high as the fifth seed. The Wizards could upset the fourth seed in a grinded-out seven games, barely coming out alive to advance for the first time since 2017. In the end, Washington falls to the powerhouse first seed in four or five games, proving it's made progress but has a ways to go.

For everything to go wrong, the Wizards' assortment of aging stars and untried youngsters must wither under raised expectations and fail to mix.

Young would have to get banged up, something he's not unfamiliar with, and contribute empty stats that look pretty but don't change results. Davis suffers an injury that sidelines him more than half the season, and his limited time on the court reflects a shell of himself from years ago.

Sarr hits a slump after a productive jump the year before, dropping his efficiency and stalling more defensive growth. Dybantsa looks like an overestimation, struggling to score anywhere outside the restricted area while Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer thrive.

With names piled on the injury list and promising prospects turned long-term projects, Washington drops to the 14th seed, just one place above its standing last year. It gets unluckier when, under the NBA's new draft lottery system, it is awarded the No. 12 pick in the draft following a poor year of trial and error.

While neither hypothetical is likely to be realized, there is one common thread that makes them possible: Anthony Davis' health. Can the 33-year-old, who has played a total of 71 games in the past two seasons, stay on the court?

It's hard to deny his production when active, even with the accumulated physical toll on his body through the years. Teams are better on both sides of the floor when he's on it because of his All-NBA caliber talent. But how regularly will he lace up his game-day shoes?

Davis is the key to the Wizards' 2026-27 season success.

The post Washington Wizards 2026-27 Preseason Preview appeared first on The Lead.

title: USF coach Brian Hartline questions authenticity of UTSA's crowd noise: 'I don't know how it gets so loud'
description: As UTSA prepares to host South Florida on Thursday, Hartline became the latest to question the acoustics of the Alamodome environment.
fullText:
Asked how he was preparing his team for the challenges of playing in the Alamodome, South Florida coach Brian Hartline became the latest UTSA opponent to question the authenticity of the Roadrunners' crowd noise.

Speaking at his Monday news conference ahead of USF's trip to face UTSA at 6:30 p.m. Thursday, Hartline mused about the connection between the Roadrunners' attendance figures - averaging about 25,000 through the first two games of 2026 - and the sound the fans create.

"I've heard that it's really loud there. I'm trying to figure out what the population size is," Hartline said. "I don't know how it gets so loud if there's not a lot of people there."

UTSA is 35-5 at home compared to a 22-22 mark on the road under seventh-year coach Jeff Traylor, ranking near the top of the American Conference and in the top 10 of the country for home victories through that span. The Roadrunners finished seventh in the league in attendance last year at 24,361 fans per game.

As one of just four indoor venues that regularly hosts FBS football, the Alamodome presents opponents with different acoustics compared to the experience of the average college football game.

Even with an announced crowd of 17,109 - UTSA's second-lowest total of the past five years - for a Sept. 26 matchup against Colorado State, the Rams were whistled for five false start penalties.

"We have never needed to pump in artificial crowd noise because our fans are so passionate that they make the Alamodome the best home field advantage in the American Conference," a UTSA spokesperson said in a statement. "We encourage our fans to come show South Florida just how loud they can be by coming out in force on Thursday and screaming their heads off every time South Florida is on offense."

Hartline is not the first to question the integrity of the Alamodome's operations.

Before Houston traveled to face UTSA in the 2022 season opener, then-Cougars coach Dana Holgorsen made a similar accusation during a radio interview.

"There's rumors they pump crowd noise into their speakers and artificially make that thing as loud as they can, which is against NCAA rules," Holgorsen said.

Then-Tulane coach Jon Sumrall also questioned the Alamodome sound before last year's trip to face UTSA on Oct. 30.

"I think they may pipe some in through the speakers," Sumrall said. "I don't think it's legal. I don't think anybody's investigating it. We've just got to be ready to deal with it. That's helped them create a home-field advantage."

After the Roadrunners scored the highlight of the season with a 48-26 win against a Green Wave team that eventually qualified for the College Football Playoff, Traylor said he felt Sumrall had been "disrespectful" and "a little more personal" during the buildup to the game.

"A coach that said we basically have been cheating the last six years, which disrespects everything we've done in this place for six year, in my opinion," Traylor said.

There's more to San Antonio with the Express-News.

title: Mike Vrabel Throws Major Shade at Bills Star After Patriots’ Week 4 Win
description: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson has never been one to bite his tongue.The outspoken defensive back typically speaks his mind with zero regard for offending anyone. It was no different after Sunday’s 29-26 loss to the division rival New England Patriots when he took a jab at Pats receiver Efton Chism, who scored the game-winning […] The post Mike Vrabel Throws Major Shade at Bills Star After Patriots’ Week 4 Win appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson has never been one to bite his tongue.

The outspoken defensive back typically speaks his mind with zero regard for offending anyone. It was no different after Sunday's 29-26 loss to the division rival New England Patriots when he took a jab at Pats receiver Efton Chism, who scored the game-winning touchdown in the final two minutes.

"Listen, we're not going to get into no bulletin-board material," Gardner-Johnson told reporters. "An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won't hear from him again. Respectfully. And I say that with a lot of confidence because… [Drake Maye] didn't put his confidence in his best player. He would've thrown it to [Romeo] Doubs or something. But they won the game. Whatever.

"They didn't do s–t better than us. We gotta play better. And they can mark that. We'll be back to see them again at the end of the year, so they can have that same energy. And they put up, what, 20-something points? They barely scored, they struggled all game. A practice-squad player made a hell of a play."

Gardner-Johnson's remarks didn't quite sit right with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, who returned the favor on Monday by taking a subtle shot right back at the 28-year-old DB.

Vrabel is another one who's not known for holding back. He has a reputation for rubbing people the wrong way sometimes, and he's usually one to let you know exactly what's on his mind.

So when he was asked about Gardner-Johnson's comments about Chism during an appearance on "The Greg Hill Show" on Monday morning, Vrabel didn't pass up the opportunity to throw some shade right back.

"For a guy who's been on eight teams in four years, I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel said.

It should be noted that Chism hasn't been on a practice squad and has been on New England's 53-man roster all season. He signed with the team as an undrafted free agent last year and won a spot on the 53-man roster. Chism played in 8 games in 2025 and he's appeared in three games this season.

Gardner-Johnson, however, was on the Baltimore Ravens practice squad just last year.

He's bounced around the league after being selected by the New Orleans Saints in the fourth round back in 2019. Since then he's had stints with the Philadelphia Eagles (two), Detroit Lions, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens, Chicago Bears, and the Bills.

title: Former PGA Tour staple course finds new home as part of LPGA's new Hawaii swing
description: The Plantation Course at Kapalua was a PGA Tour staple for 25 years.
fullText:
The Plantation Course at Kapalua was a PGA Tour staple for 25 years, hosting the Sentry, which served as the kickoff event from 1999 to 2013 and again from 2024 to 2025. That relationship ended in April when the PGA Tour announced it planned to end its tournament presence in Maui.

But while the PGA Tour won't be returning to the Plantation Course next year, Kapalua now has a new professional golf partner in the LPGA.

On Monday, the LPGA announced that the Lotte Championship will be hosted at the Plantation Course starting in 2027. The tournament, which Jeeno Thitikul won on Sunday, will now be held in March as part of a two-tournament Hawaii Swing along with the recently announced Nanea Cup. The Lotte Championship will have a $3 million purse next season.

"We are thrilled to have Kapalua Resort and the Plantation Course serve as the venue for the Lotte Championship in 2027. As we continue to strengthen the LPGA tour schedule, venues with deep-rooted heritage like Kapalua are exactly what we look for," LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler said in a release. "This new chapter would not be possible without the support and commitment to the tour that Lotte and Kapalua provided. We want to thank Hoakalei Country Club for the last five years and look forward to building on the success of the Lotte Championship at its new home in Maui."

This will be the first time Kapalua has hosted an LPGA event since the 2008 Kapalua LPGA Classic, which Morgan Pressel won.

Want to see the LPGA's future? 'Scrappy' Nelly Korda plan offers a glimpse

The newly created Hawaii Swing is part of Kessler's broader vision to remake the LPGA schedule into one that makes logistical sense and is centered on golf courses, prize money and routing.

"On schedule, hopefully you've heard us talk about routing, courses and purses. We are ruthless on all three of those fronts," Kessler said of his plan at last year's CME Group Tour Championship. "We know we've got some more work to do on courses and purses, and we have the mindset of continuous improvement, and every year you should expect us to get just a little bit better on all three of those dimensions."

Kessler and the LPGA have worked this year to improve the outlook for the schedule going forward.

The LPGA Corning Classic is also returning to western New York after an 18-year absence. It was an LPGA fixture for 31 years before ending in 2009.

"The return of the Classic brings together the LPGA's history and its future. As we continue shaping the next chapter of our Tour, we're building on the qualities that have defined the LPGA for decades — incredible championships, committed partners, passionate communities and unforgettable experiences for our athletes," Kessler said of bringing back the Corning Classic.

The LPGA, LET and Golf Saudi will also co-sanction an event in London in 2027 with a $4 million purse.

But the biggest swing Kessler has taken on the new schedule is the creation of the Nanea Cup, which will involve a mix of top LPGA pros and collegiate women's golfers to showcase the sport's present and future. The tournament, which will include 95 LPGA Tour players and 25 of the nation's top college golfers, will be held at David McLay Kidd's Nanea Golf Club. The LPGA will exit that event and head right to Kaplua as Kessler's new vision takes shape.

The full LPGA 2027 schedule is expected to arrive this week.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Sends Blunt Message to Fans Amid Lions Struggles
description: The Detroit Lions defense is the worst in the NFL through four weeks. While star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is having a good season, he is the leader of this unit and is taking accountability for the struggles. Hutchinson was asked what can be said by him and his teammates, not only in the locker […] The post Aidan Hutchinson Sends Blunt Message to Fans Amid Lions Struggles appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions defense is the worst in the NFL through four weeks. While star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is having a good season, he is the leader of this unit and is taking accountability for the struggles.

Hutchinson was asked what can be said by him and his teammates, not only in the locker room, but to the frustrated fans. The Lions' four-year, $180M star edge rusher made it clear that nothing can be said right now because talk is cheap."

"I'm so tired of talk," declared Hutchinson on the discussions going on in the locker room. "To me, talk is cheap. If you really want to do something, let's go win the damn game and make the plays we need to make."

Hutchinson was fired up when discussing what the team needs to do.

However, when he was asked what the team can do on paper, or within the scheme, to change things, he admitted that he is just as stumped as defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.

"I'm not sure right now," admitted Hutchinson. "I'm kind of still analyzing and trying to figure out what is going wrong."

However, Hutchinson made it clear to fans that he is not quitting on the team despite the slow start. He still sees things turning around and the team making the most of this.

"I'm going to stay in it," said Hutchinson. "I am going to keep improving individually and try to do anything I can do to help our team win."

The Lions star told fans not to quit and to stay in it with him. He noted that he sees a semblance of a dangerous team. They just need to put everything together.

"I know we're going to figure it out," said Hutchinson. "And when we do, when we're clicking on all cylinders, we're going to be such a dangerous team."

Detroit is still 2-2 despite the defense. If they can get the defense figured out, the offense is going to help them win games.

The Lions' secondary gets a lot of the bad reputation on the defense, and that is rightfully so. However, the edge rusher group outside of Hutchinson is also a disappointment.

Hutchinson has 29 pressures on 182 pass rush snaps. He has a 27.1% win rate and a 9.9 pass-rush productivity rate per PFF. D.J. Wonnum is second on the team with eight pressures on 128 pass-rush snaps.

He has a 4.7 PRP and an 11% win rate. Tyler Lacy has 51 pass rush snaps and a 3.1 PRP, with a 6.3% win rate. Lastly is rookie Derrick Moore. The second-round pick has just 29 pass rush snaps. Moore has three pressures and a 5.4 PRP. He has a disappointing 3.6% pass-rush win rate.

The secondary is a problem, but the three rushers behind Hutchinson have not carried their weight. Hutchinson can only do so much. The others need to step up.

title: The Texas-Oklahoma rivalry can change things quickly, regardless of teams' records
description: A year after Texas entered the game with two losses, the roles have flipped. Kirk Bohls explains why the Red River rivalry can turn quickly.
fullText:
AUSTIN - The storylines are pretty much the same this October.

That's how fast things can change in one of the most historic rivalries in the sport.

Texas has raised itself from the ashes after reaching the heights of the Mack Brown era. Oklahoma was running things in the Big 12 and grabbing Heisman trophies like they were pocket change before running afoul of late.

Texas reached the College Football Playoff semifinals two straight seasons from 2023-24 before sitting out the playoffs last year. OU hadn't been a contender recently but did crash the CFP party last December only to exit quickly despite leading Alabama 17-0 in Norman in the first round.

We turn to the present season. Texas is up, OU is down. But check back in a week where fortunes can change at breakneck speed.

Texas, most would probably agree, isn't the best team in college football, but it is unbeaten and ranked No. 1 because of quality wins. That's why it is a 7½-point favorite.

Oklahoma, everyone would attest, isn't close to the best team, either, or maybe not even one of the really good teams in college football, but there are few programs as proud or as successful as the Sooners, and they might actually be good with two quality losses.

And to be honest, none of that really matters when it comes to October in Dallas where Stonie Clark can become a hero with one monumental tackle at the goal-line and Peter Gardere stamps his legacy as a quarterback with four wins over OU. Players can enter the Cotton Bowl as a mortal and leave 60 minutes later as a legend.

BOHLS: Nine things and one crazy prediction

Who knows what qualifies as an upset any more in a series that has been played in Dallas since 1912 and at the State Fair since 1929 and is more passion play than sport. The Longhorns lead the series 65-51-5, but there are good reasons Texas ranks fifth in all-time football wins at 975 and OU sixth with 967.

"I can promise you one thing," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said, "nobody's overlooking anybody in this game."

That's the perfect history lesson since these two teams have flipped the scripts from just 12 months ago.

A year ago the wounded Longhorns limped into the Cotton Bowl unranked with two losses.

On Saturday, the flawed Sooners will sneak into that historic area unranked with two losses.

Before this game in 2025, Texas had lost to one of the college football foremost bluebloods on the road (Ohio State) and was embarrassed in its SEC opener (at Florida).

This year, OU has lost to one of the heavyweight brands in the nation on the road (Michigan) and was humiliated in its SEC opener (at Georgia).

While the two teams appear to be trending in opposite directions, their emotions will identically coincide this weekend. Nothing changes that.

Both squads will be at a fever pitch for Saturday's 2:45 p.m. kickoff. Actually even before that.

"There's always a ton of emotion in pregame for whatever reason," Sarkisian acknowledged. "The ball's not kicked off, and everybody's all hyped up at the start of the game."

Sarkisian said he and his staff will try to temper those emotions, nerves and unbridled anticipation and stay focused on the game itself.

Texas didn't do that all that well last October when it trailed 6-3 at intermission, but rallied to shut out the Sooners 20-0 in the second half to seal its second consecutive win in this series and third in four years.

That's usually how this series flows. One side dominates for a span, only to be ultimately switched. Just ask Mack Brown.

Sarkisian doesn't really He attributes the Sooners' 2-2 record largely to being a product of a harsh schedule, but of course the last thing he wants to do is rile up the crimson fan base.

"I don't know that necessarily they haven't played well," said Sarkisian, who is personally 3-2 against the Sooners. "Defensively, they've played exceptional. These guys are a phenomenal defensive football team. They played at Michigan, which is not easy. They played at Georgia, which we know is not easy. I'm sure Coach (Brent) Venables wishes he had the schedule of some other teams or they could be 4-0."

While the Longhorns appear to have much more to play for with a terrific start at a championship run with two quality wins over Ohio State and Tennessee, the Sooners will approach this game with an anger level and desperation that could mask any shortage of offensive firepower or momentum.

Mix in a slow start with a turnover here and there, and up may become down. Worked for Texas last year.

That's just how this rivalry rolls.

"They're definitely going to give us their best effort," Longhorn linebacker Justin Cryer said. "I think they are super dynamic (on offense). But I don't take a lot from their recent performances and people's perception of them. This is a game they're going to show up for. We have to be on it or it's going to be a long day for us."

That type of response has to be music to Sarkisian's ears.

He gave his players, which include 48 newcomers to his roster, a tutorial on Texas-OU 101 to educate them about the history and significance of the only rivalry in the country that splits the stadium down the middle with rival fans sitting side by side at the two 50-yard lines. You know, within spitting range.

Heck, he even showed them a picture of the storied Cotton Bowl and pointed out the tunnel from which both teams enter the playing field and where they will warm up.

"But at the end of the day," he said, "it's football, and the game means a ton to us. I don't waste a lot of time and energy in the rah-rah speeches on a Monday."

For his money, he loves the neutral-site setting of this game, which will be played for the 122nd time. Thankfully, he appreciates the history and doesn't ever want to go to a home-and-home arrangement.

"The idea that this thing's split at the 50, and half the game is a home game, and the other time it's a road game when you're in OU's end, I love all of that," Sarkisian said. "I love all that comes with it. I love that it's at the State Fair. The smell of the corn dogs, the funnel cakes and all that, it's so special and so unique, and I do not take that lightly. I would not change it for anything."

That's one thing that should never change, even if the programs' trajectories do.

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle.

title: J.J. McCarthy Giants Week 5 News Revealed by John Harbaugh
description: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh revealed that newly acquired QB J.J. McCarthy could be the backup quarterback in Week 5.McCarthy was acquired by the Giants last week from the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round draft pick in 2027.In Week 4, McCarthy dressed as the third-string QB behind starting QB Jameis Winston and backup […] The post J.
fullText:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh revealed that newly acquired QB J.J. McCarthy could be the backup quarterback in Week 5.

McCarthy was acquired by the Giants last week from the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round draft pick in 2027.

In Week 4, McCarthy dressed as the third-string QB behind starting QB Jameis Winston and backup QB Jake Haener.

According to the Giants' head coach, when speaking to the media on Monday, Harbaugh said that McCarthy may be elevated to backup QB behind Winston for Week 5 against the Washington Commanders.

"I think that's a possibility. We'll see how it goes during the week, but that's definitely on the table," Harbaugh said.

J.J. McCarthy could be the Giants' QB2 for their Week 5 matchup against the Commanders pic.twitter.com/LUBt0qIoEg

— SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 5, 2026

The Giants lost their starting quarterback, Jaxson Dart, during their Week 2 game against the Los Angeles Rams due to a knee injury that will keep him out for the rest of the season.

With Dart out, Winston has been starting for New York the last two weeks, and he has led the team to two wins over the Tennessee Titans and the Arizona Cardinals despite having poor numbers.

The Giants could definitely use an upgrade at the QB position — even though Winston helped the team win games in Weeks 3 and 4 — which is where McCarthy may come into play.

Although things did not work out well for the former 10th-overall draft pick with the Vikings, he is still only 23 years old and has untapped potential in the sport, which he could possibly unleash with the Giants — if he gets the chance to start, that is.

For now, the next step for McCarthy in his Giants' career would be getting to back up Winston in Week 5 against the Commanders and see where things go from there.

Knowing he could potentially be put into game action if Winston goes down with an injury shows that Harbaugh and the Giants' coaching staff are liking what they are seeing from him in practice if they are willing to bump him ahead of Haener in the team's quarterback depth chart.

title: Bengals Get Mixed Injury News on Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins
description: The Cincinnati Bengals are still waiting for clarity on the status of their two biggest offensive weapons ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Miami Dolphins.Both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were forced out of Cincinnati’s 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, leaving the team without either star receiver for the final […] The post Bengals Get Mixed Injury News on Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals are still waiting for clarity on the status of their two biggest offensive weapons ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Miami Dolphins.

Both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were forced out of Cincinnati's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, leaving the team without either star receiver for the final stretch of the game.

Bengals head coach Zac Taylor provided an update on both players Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Chase remains in the NFL's concussion protocol, while Higgins is now considered day-to-day with the adductor injury he suffered against Jacksonville.

Bengals HC Zac Taylor said WR Ja’Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol, and Tee Higgins is now considered day-to day due to his adductor injury.

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 5, 2026

This update leaves the status of both receivers uncertain as Cincinnati prepares to head to Miami. The Bengals will get a better idea of where things stand when they return to practice and release their first injury report of the week.

Chase's status is the bigger unknown because he is in the NFL's concussion protocol. He will need to progress through the NFL's five-step return-to-participation process and receive final clearance before he can suit up Sunday.

The All-Pro receiver suffered the injury during the second quarter against Jacksonville. Chase caught a pass from Joe Burrow before Jaguars cornerback Jarrian Jones grabbed his facemask during the tackle. Chase then took another hit and went to the ground.

He was evaluated on the field before walking to the blue medical tent and eventually heading to the locker room. The Bengals later ruled him out with a concussion.

Chase finished the game with 3 receptions and 27 yards. His absence forced the Bengals to adjust and rely more on Higgins and Dohnte Meyers.

Taylor confirmed after the game that Chase had suffered a concussion, but Monday's update did not provide a timetable for his return. His progress through the protocol will now be something to watch throughout the week.

Chase is a difficult player to replace for a Bengals team that desperately needs a win after dropping two in a row. His status throughout the week will be worth monitoring.

There is at least a little more clarity surrounding Higgins.

The Bengals initially announced that Higgins suffered an adductor injury late in Sunday's loss. Taylor said after the game that Higgins attempted to return despite the injury but was unable to continue. "He knew the situation we were in. He just couldn't do it," Taylor said of Higgins' attempt to return.

Higgins was having a big day before the injury, hauling in 11 passes for 157 yards. He paced the team in yards and tied Chase Brown for the most receptions.

Higgins' status being day-to-day, as reported by Schefter, is a somewhat encouraging development, though it doesn't guarantee his availability for Sunday.

Cincinnati's receiver depth was tested against Jacksonville. While Burrow put up 428 yards and nearly led a late game comeback, the Bengals could not get in the end zone on their final drive. If Higgins and/or Chase miss any time, expect Dohnte Meyers and Mitch Tinsley to see more snaps out wide. Also keep an eye out for the status of rookie Colbie Young. He was ruled out against Jacksonville but could provide a boost to the WR corps.

The status of Chase and Higgins will be at the top of mind this week as the Bengals will look to end their two-game losing streak in Miami.

Devin Booker and forward Dillon Brooks provided outlooks for the game, which can be seen on Arizona's Family (3TV) in the Phoenix area.

"Play hard, play together, share basketball and see how our defense stands up to one of the best teams last year in the paint and rebounding."

"I think defense, rebound, and close in possession is, you know, a point of emphasis for us last year, and, you know, there's no better team to test it against the Pistons that play hard. They're top 5 and offensive rebounds last year. So, you know, defending the whole shot clock, communicating with each other and finishing possessions."

Booker said the majority of training camp has been focused on defending.

The Suns finished ninth in the NBA in defensive rating last season, but they were 13th from March 1 to the end of the 2025-26 regular season.

"If we're going to be a red group, communicating those reds loud and early, being a physical team, being the first to fight, all the things that help you win," Booker added.

Here are three more things to watch Monday night.

Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach are competing for the starting center position as Mark Williams will miss several months with a left shoulder injury (torn labrum).

Ighodaro will get the start, Monday, Suns coach Jordan Ott said.

"Remember they're young players, but all these possessions are valuable to us as we evaluate during the preseason into regular season," Ott said. "We need both of them."

The Suns are starting Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges and Ighodaro in the preseason opener.

Pistons All-Star big Jalen Duren isn't playing. He just signed a five-year deal for $200 million deal with Detroit. The Pistons are looking to ramp him up for their season opener, Oct. 20, against the Boston Celtics.

He would've been a good test for Ighodaro and Maluach, but the Pistons are playing it smart with him.

"We've got a plan."

Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff on ramping up Jalen Duren, who just signed a $200M deal. 

Said Duren is in great shape, but they're going to be patient with him.

Duren won't be available for tonight's preseason opener vs Phoenix Suns. #Suns #Pistons pic.twitter.com/FMOIYahwKr

Ighodaro and Maluach have been saying the right things. The competition is making each other better.

Ighodaro is a passer, screener and ball handler who can finish at the rim.

The Suns can run more of their perimeter offense with Ighodaro because he can serve as a hub, but Maluach puts pressure on the rim with his rolls and has 3-point range to give them a pick-and-pop element.

Phoenix may have different combinations with each player because they each have such different skill sets. Look to see who plays with each one.

Jordan Ott on Suns bigs Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach as Ighodaro will start tonight vs. Pistons: "Remember they're young players, but all these possessions are valuable to us as we evaluate during the preseason into regular season, we need both of them."

Said Suns must find… pic.twitter.com/2r44L3XHJv

Ott said the Suns are looking to find a third big to go along with Maluach and Ighodaro.

CJ Huntley is a two-way player in his second season, while Duop Reath is a training camp invite who is entering his fourth NBA season.

Ott added the Suns will look at a non-traditional five.

"That's a little bit in the preseason," Ott said. "Who our third big is. Where do we go? We have young wings. Can we play with a non-traditional five a little bit, which will probably end up seeing today if the rotation goes accordingly."

That could be Miles Bridges or Haywood Highsmith. Both have the bulk to guard bigger bodies.

Rookie Koa Peat may get a look in that non-traditional lineup as well, but this is more about who the Suns will keep on that 15-man roster between Highsmith, Huntley and Reath.

They could keep Huntley, sign Reath to a two-way contract, as this is the last year of eligibility for him to have one and release Huntley and have him play for their G League team, the Valley Suns, as the Suns did last season with Huntley.

Khaman Maluach and Duop Reath for 3. #Suns pic.twitter.com/Zt6IIVYbUc

Booker said during training camp that Jalen Green and Bridges are looking to provide playmaking this season.

Bridges may be 

"I know Miles is an unselfish player," Brooks said. "Does everything from the gritty stuff to hit the open 3. That's going to be key for our offense. And JG, once he figures out how to play-make in the offense, because he only had maybe 30, 40 games to play last year, he's going to be able to find better holes to drive the lane, more shots for him as well. With those guys being our primary playmakers, they'll be able to get their shots on the back end."

title: Skesterkin named NHL 1st Star of Week after historic Rangers goalie goal
description: Scoring the first goalie goal in New York Rangers history comes with some perks. Igor Shesterkin claimed top billing among […]
fullText:
Scoring the first goalie goal in New York Rangers history comes with some perks. Igor Shesterkin claimed top billing among the NHL's Three Stars for the week ending Oct. 4 after making 71 saves and recording two points in the League's opening week.

The Rangers goalie was named First Star, edging out Edmonton Oilers defenseman Evan Bouchard (four goals, eight points in three games) and Vancouver Cancucks forward Paul Cotter (four goals, six points in four games), who earned Second and Third Star honors, respectively.

Igor Shesterkin, Evan Bouchard, Paul Cotter named "Three Stars" for the week ending Oct. 4.

3 Stars of the Week presented by @GEICO#NHLStats: https://t.co/UiUWXEyLWV pic.twitter.com/YQfgn06oni

— NHL Public Relations (@NHLPR) October 5, 2026

Shesterkin scored his first career NHL goal Thursday, helping New York secure its first win of the 2026-27 season, 5-1 over the Tampa Bay Lightning.

With fellow countryman Andrei Vasilevskiy pulled in favor of the extra attacker, Shesterkin corralled a long Lightning pass off the end boards and sent a high-arcing shot back toward the Tampa Bay zone. The puck crossed the goal line inside the left post with 2:34 left in the third period, prompting a roar from the Madison Square Garden crowd and fist bumps from his Blueshirts teammates along the bench.

"That was a top moment for me in my career for sure," Rangers captain J.T. Miller said Thursday. "And it was the first time I've ever been a part of something like that."

Shesterkin had an opportunity to find the back of the net again Sunday when the Utah Mammoth pulled goalie Karel Vejmelka with 1:45 left in the third trailing 2-1.

"I thought he was gonna score again," coach Mike Sullivan chuckled postgame.

THE FIRST RANGERS GOALTENDER TO SCORE A GOAL:

IGOR SHESTERKIN pic.twitter.com/k7ITHnvtza

— New York Rangers (@NYRangers) October 2, 2026

The Garden crowd egged him on. Chants of "shoot" echoed through the building as soon as Shesterkin vacated his net to play the puck in the trapezoid. Instead, he extended his point streak to two games with a secondary assist, sliding the puck up the boards to Will Cuylle, who moved it ahead to Eeli Tolvanen for an empty-net goal to seal a 3-1 win.

But his offensive feats shouldn't overshadow his stellar play in net. Shesterkin is 2-10 with a 1.67 goals-against average and .934 save percentage through three games, and ranks second in the NHL with 71 saves. He held Nikita Kucherov and the Lightning to one goal on 24 shots Thursday and stopped 28 of 30 shots against previously undefeated Utah.

Reliable goaltending is a luxury in the NHL. The Rangers have enjoyed it for the better part of three decades.

Mike Richter manned New York's crease from 1989 until 2003 and helped bring the Stanley Cup Trophy back to Broadway in 1994. Henrik Lundqvist followed, and while he never lifted a Cup during his 15-year NHL career, the Rangers' all-time leader in wins (459) put together a stellar career that rightfully earned him a place in the Hockey Hall of Fame. They don't call him "The King" for nothing.

Shesterkin had big skates to fill as Lundqvist's successor, but he has proved more than up to the task.

The 30-year-old netminder topped The Athletic's NHL goalie rankings for the third straight season — a testament to his continued excellence. Shesterkin has received Vezina votes in four of six seasons since 2020 and ran away with the award in 2022 after posting a 2.07 GAA and .935 save percentage in 53 games.

His puck-handling ability is an added bonus, and a weapon in itself.

"I don't think there's any question that it's a competitive advantage," Sullivan said Monday at practice. "In today's game, with how aggressive the forechecks are, when you have a goaltender that has the ability to play the puck like Shesty does, it's a huge advantage for your team."

It's not hard to see why the Rangers locked up Shesterkin through 2032-33 on an eight-year, $92.48 million extension — a deal that's looking more and more like a bargain as the NHL salary cap rises.

title: Kentucky football coach Will Stein is step for step with Bear Bryant
description: Will Stein is the first Kentucky coach to start his maiden campaign 4-1 since Bear Bryant. Stein's challenge is to continue keeping pace with Bryant.
fullText:
COLUMBIA, SC — Before Kentucky football welcomed Alabama to Lexington in Week 2 of the season, Paul Finebaum, a man known for making bold proclamations on the regular, offered up yet another.

"Seventy-five years ago, Bear Bryant coached at the University of Kentucky," Finebaum said Sept. 12 on the set of SEC Nation. "I feel a vibe right now that the next Bear Bryant has showed up at Kentucky."

A coach so iconic, his nickname stands on its own more than four decades since his death. Quite a comparison for 37-year-old, first-time head coach Will Stein.

Attention-grabbing? To be sure.

Inaccurate? The long-term returns are still to be determined. But in the short term? Stein — somehow — is step for step with Bear. With a stunning 35-34 overtime victory against South Carolina on Oct. 3, Stein is 4-1 in his first season as UK's coach. The last coach to achieve that feat? Yeah.

His list of accomplishments are so vast, it would take all day to list them. Six national titles. Fourteen SEC championships. More than 300 wins. Stein has four victories ... and none of those other crowns.

For now, he's trying to match what Bryant did well before his legendary run at Alabama began.

Bryant remains the only coach in Kentucky history to lead the program to a New Year's Six bowl game. He did so in three consecutive seasons. The Orange Bowl in 1949. The Sugar Bowl in 1950. And the Cotton Bowl in 1951. An appearance in any of those bowls this season means the Wildcats have done the unthinkable — all of those bowls are part of the College Football Playoff.

The 12 teams in this year's playoff field won't be announced for another two months. Between now and then, Kentucky has seven more regular-season games. Its next, on paper, will be its toughest. No. 11 LSU (4-1, 1-1 SEC) and the Lane Kiffin Train roll into Lexington for a 7 p.m. kickoff Oct. 10.

Kentucky won't be favored to win.

But it wasn't expected to beat a top-10 Texas A&M team last month. (Final score: UK 31, A&M 21.)

It wasn't expected to beat South Carolina, either. (You already know the final score by now.)

For many longtime followers of the sport, the thought of Kentucky as a playoff team is still absurd.

Let their critics think that, players say.

"We're here. We're doing great things, and we've just got to continue to prove that each and every Saturday," senior defensive back Ty Bryant said. (No relation to Bear, if you're wondering.) "And if they want to stay asleep (on us)? They can do that."

Level-headed quarterback Kenny Minchey also had no interest in thinking too far ahead.

"I feel like that's something that people in media try to paint on a team — it just happens to be our team — (that) may start (a season) fast or start slow. ... We just want to go 1-0 each week," Minchey said. "And now our focus is, enjoy this win, but tomorrow we got to go to the doctor and then get ready for our next opponent."

Talk of a "one-play mentality" was the company line from Stein and his players after Saturday's win, which saw the team overcome a 17-0 deficit. It was the largest come-from-behind road triumph in the Wildcats' record book. Not surprisingly, that's what Minchey cited as the primary reason for the victory. And the 4-1 start.

"It's easy to either look back or look forward," he said. "It's hard to really focus on right now."

For players and coaches? That's fine and dandy. Focus on the here and now.

Those outside the locker room can hem and haw about the past. In Kentucky's case, one that has far too often been about a team occupying the SEC's cellar. In turn, that's why those same outsiders want to ponder the Wildcats' future. Perhaps one that, like border neighbor Indiana, includes Kentucky as a playoff participant.

If that comes to pass, comparing Stein to Bear will look less and less outlandish.

Reach Kentucky men's basketball and football reporter Ryan Black at rblack@gannett.com and follow him on X at @RyanABlack.

title: Oregon LB commit Brayton Feister ruled ineligible to play by OHSAA
description: Oregon commit Brayton Feister was ruled ineligible for the rest of his high school senior season in Ohio after transferring schools in the offseason.
fullText:
One of the Oregon Ducks' top commitments in the 2027 recruiting class might be done for the rest of his senior season in high school. Brayton Feister, who committed to the Ducks in August, was ruled ineligible by the Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) on Monday.

Feister, alongside his younger brother, Brydon, was ruled ineligible for the second half of the season at Massillon Washington High School after transferring between school years. The Canton Repository, part of the USA TODAY Network, first reported the news.

The Feister brothers will challenge the ruling on Tuesday in a court hearing in Stark County. The older Feister is a star running back and linebacker who is committed as a linebacker with the Ducks. As a junior at Archbishop Hoban, Feister made 133 tackles with 39 tackles for loss and 13 sacks. As a running back, Feister had 1,098 rushing yards and 17 touchdowns.

Massillon is undefeated this season, but the Tuesday court hearing could determine the eligibility of six transfer players, including the Feisters. The OSHAA ruling covered three of the six players, approving eligibility for one other player. However, the preliminary injunction hearing on Tuesday could extend, alter or end a temporary restraining order that allowed the six players to play, which was issued on Sept. 25 by a Stark County Common Pleas Court judge.

The OHSAA ruled the Feister brothers ineligible after arguing that the brothers did not qualify for an athletic eligibility exception because the Feister family's move to Massillon was driven by a desire to transfer schools following disciplinary issues at the state wrestling championships. The OSHAA also alleged that Feister's father contacted other schools about enrollment before making the move to Massillon.

The 6-foot-2 linebacker is the No. 131 player in the 2027 recruiting class, per Rivals, and is part of Oregon's class, which ranks No. 4 in the nation. He chose the Ducks over California, Georgia and Ohio State. Feister is one of four linebackers in Oregon's class and could compete for early playing time next season, but his status on the field as a high school senior is worth monitoring.
